sentences.text:
This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the claimant questioning the judgment and award passed in MVC No.1018/2017 dated 24.03.2021 by the Additional Small Causes and Senior Civil Judge and MACT,
Mysuru (for short referred to as 'Tribunal') on the ground of inadequate and meager compensation awarded by the tribunal.

2. The claimant was traveling in a TVS Star City Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-09-EV-4412 on 22.06.2017 at about 10:30 p.m., on Nanjangud - Gundalpet road towards Kasuvinahalli on the left side of the road, during NC: 2024:KHC:7763 which time, a Hero Honda Splendor Plus Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-10-L-1232 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the two wheeler of the claimant and due to which, the claimant suffered injuries to both bones of right leg and he was immediately shifted to JSS hospital, where he underwent operation and implants were inserted to his right leg.
He took treatment as an inpatient for a period of 11 days.
Due to the occurrence of the accident, the claimant has been disabled permanently and he has lost his future financial earning capacity.
Hence, he filed a claim petition seeking enhancement of compensation.
3. The respondent No.1 though served, did not file statement of objections.

The respondent No.2/insurance company filed statement of objections denying the claim of the claimant including age, avocation and income of the claimant and the negligence attributed as against the rider of the offending vehicle and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. The claimant in order to substantiate his claim examined himself as PW.1, he examined doctor as PW.2 and NC: 2024:KHC:7763 exhibited documents as Exs.P1 to P18.
The respondents neither adduced evidence nor produced any documents.

On the basis of the materials placed before the Court, the tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.2,82,500/- along with interest at 6% per Jagadish vs Shivakumar D B on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45635766/
2 annum and directed the respondent to deposit the compensation amount within 30 days from the date of award.
5. Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation.
6.
I have heard the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2/insurance company and perused the impugned judgment and award.

7. Exs.P1 to P7 are the police records which depict filing of an FIR and a charge sheet against the rider of the offending vehicle which is not questioned or controverted and no material is placed before this Court to substantiate the same.
Exs.P8 to 18 are the medical records to show the employment of claimant, the salary slip and the expenditures NC: 2024:KHC:7763 met by the claimant towards his treatment.
On perusal of these records, negligence is rightly attributed as against the rider of the offending vehicle.

8. Now coming to the question of age, avocation, income, disability and multiplier, the age of the claimant was taken as 31 years as on date of occurrence of the accident, the appropriate multiplier applicable would be '16' which has been rightly adopted by the tribunal.
The tribunal has taken the income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.13,000/- per month on the basis of Exs.P11 and P12 and the same is retained.

The doctor has been examined as PW.2 who has opined that the claimant has suffered permanent physical disability to right lower limb to an extent of 23.65%, the tribunal has considered the evidence of doctor and has assessed the disability at 8% which does not call for interference.
Therefore, the loss of future earning capacity due to the disability is not interfered and the same is retained.
9. Towards pain and suffering the tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- which is on the lower side, hence, an additional sum of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under this NC: 2024:KHC:7763 head.

Towards loss of income during laid up period, the tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.26,000/-,
considering the rest taken for a period of two months.
But considering the fractures sustained by the claimant, minimum three months time is required to recover from the injuries and get back to normal day to day activities.
Hence, a sum of Rs.39,000/- is awarded under this head.

Towards food and nourishment, attendant charges a sum of Rs.5,500/- was awarded by the tribunal, whereas the claimant was inpatient for a period of 11 days, hence, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.11,000/- under this head.
A sum of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities, which is on the lower side, hence, an additional sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under the said head.
Towards medical expenses a sum of Rs.31,000/- is awarded and the same is retained.
10. In view of the above discussions, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.3,36,000/- as against Rs.2,82,500/-.

11. Accordingly I pass the following:

entities.text: 2024:KHC:7763 ORDER Jagadish vs Shivakumar D B
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The judgment and award passed by the tribunal in MVC No.1018/2017 dated 24.03.2021 is modified and the claimant is entitled for a compensation of Rs.3,36,000/- along with interest at 6% per annum.
(iii) The enhanced compensation shall be paid within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
(iv) Entire compensation amount shall be disbursed and released in favour of the claimant upon proper identification.
Sd/-
